note: Candidates checked during the 2026-08-14 verify pass against the ICNF register (portugal-icnf.json, 49 entries within 20km). Kept as data per Hidde's 2026-08-03 standing rule that nothing researched should be wasted. Never rendered: these are leads/blocked, not entries.

leads.name: The Taxodium distichum (Swamp Cypress) of Quinta de Monserrate
leads.reason: treesandshrubsonline.org (International Dendrology Society) states 'one of 33.5m x 1.5m dbh at Quinta de Monserrate, Sintra (Portugal)', citing '(Monumental Trees 2025; Jacobson 1996)'. Checked directly (fetched, not a search summary) but the citation for this specific figure traces to Monumental Trees, and Jacobson 1996 ('North American Landscape Trees') is unlikely to independently cover a Portuguese specimen rather than the general Taxodium/US context the surrounding paragraph discusses. No second source independent of Monumental Trees found this pass (checked ISA/Lisbon's own Taxodium page and general Portuguese nursery/species pages, none mention Monserrate specifically). Does not clear the two-source bar today; would ship if a future pass finds Franco 1951-style independent botanical literature or an official Parques de Sintra page naming this specimen, the same route that worked for sin_006's kauri.

leads.name: Podocarpus neriifolius, grounds of Pena Palace
leads.reason: treesandshrubsonline.org carries only a photo caption: 'Podocarpus neriifolius (as labelled) in the grounds of the Pena Palace, Sintra, Portugal. 12 June 2012. Image Tom Christian.' No measurement, no age, no precise location, and 'as labelled' hints at taxonomic uncertainty. Too thin to write up; a future pass could try contacting/searching for a fuller record if the photographer or Parques de Sintra ever published one.

leads.name: The two sequoias near Tanque dos Frades, Parque da Pena (carried over, unchanged)
leads.species: Sequoia sp. or Sequoiadendron sp., unconfirmed
leads.reason: Carried over from the 2026-09-13 note below: a travel article (viagens.sapo.pt) claims 'two enormous sequoias' near Tanque dos Frades among the first specimens from the mid-19th-century reforestation, but parquesdesintra.pt's own page for that recanto does not mention sequoias at all. No measurement, age or coordinate for either tree. Re-checked this pass (no new source found); still too thin and still conflicting on species.

blocked.name: The Abies x vasconcellosiana type trees, Parque da Pena
blocked.species: Abies gamblei (described from Sintra material as Abies x vasconcellosiana by Franco, 1946)
blocked.reason: treesandshrubsonline.org (International Dendrology Society, fetched directly) records that Franco described this taxon in 1946 from trees growing in Pena Park, Sintra, then about 40 years old and c. 20m tall, but states plainly that 'the original trees upon which he based his description had all died by 1995'. Genuinely historically interesting (Sintra's microclimate produced a naturally-occurring hybrid fir once distributed to major European collections as propagated material) but the specific specimens are confirmed dead for three decades. Never ships as an entry per the standing dead-tree rule; recorded here so a future pass does not re-chase it as a live candidate. Worth a mention in a future STORY pass on sin_001 (the same park) as scientific colour, not as its own tree.

blocked.name: The Sweet Chestnut of Quinta do Castanheiro
blocked.register_ref: portugal-icnf.json, D.G. n.º 70, II Serie de 26/03/1945, girth 9.6m, age_register 800 (last measured 1989)
blocked.reason: Re-confirmed exclusion, not a new finding: this exact tree was already checked and excluded when Sintra first shipped (2026-07-28, recorded in archive/CURATION-2026-07.md and archive/LOG-2026-07.md). It stands at Quinta do Castanheiro on private land, and press coverage recorded it mutilated in February 2025 with declassification recommended. Hard rule on private land plus an unresolved vitality question after known mutilation. Does not come back without a source confirming both public access and that the tree survived the mutilation in recoverable condition.

blocked.name: The plane trees of Largo do Infante D. Henrique, Colares
blocked.register_ref: portugal-icnf.json, three entries tagged tipo=Arvore isolada, girths 4.12m/4.58m/1.88m, age_register 120/120/30, no classified decree recorded
blocked.reason: Not a single collectible point. Sintra Noticias (2022-03-20) and a local blog (riodasmacas.blogspot.com, 2021-03) both describe Colares' plane trees as one continuous roadside planting ("conjunto arboreo", officially 33 plataneiros classified together 2020-01-28) running "from the Varzea bridge to the Banzao on the road to the beach", fronting the Adega Regional de Colares. The three register entries near Largo do Infante D. Henrique / Restaurante D'A Varzea are administratively tagged isolated but sit at the same Varzea site the sources describe as part of the row; no source draws a clean boundary marking these three as a separate compact ensemble distinct from the avenue. Reads as the same non-collectible-point case as Barcelona's La Rambla planes (already blocked project-wide) rather than a walkable cluster addition. Also 4.2km from Sintra's existing 3.1km-span cluster (Colares is its own village; day-trip-only if it ever ships), which was the brief's own reason to deprioritize it below the castanheiro. Leave blocked unless a future pass finds a source that clearly separates these three as a standalone, named square distinct from the avenue.
blocked.also_note: Two other candidates from the brief's 35-unmined list were checked and found to be duplicates already published, not leads: the 0.8km sobreiro (Quercus suber, girth 4.75m/register vs 4.8m brief rounding, age 350) at 38.79621,-9.39565 is sin_002 (The Fern Cork Oak of Quinta do Relogio, 38.796,-9.396, ~38m away, matches on species/girth/age/classification decree D.R. n. 276 1996 exactly). The 1.5km platano (Platanus hybrida, girth 7.71m, age 200) at 38.79560,-9.38590 is sin_003 (The Plane Tree of Parque da Liberdade, 38.796,-9.386, ~45m away, matches on species/girth/age/decree D.G. n. 290 1951 exactly). data/research/sintra-register-candidates.json had already flagged both near_published matches before this pass started.

blocked.name: The Quinta do Senhor da Serra cluster (plane avenue, yew, two box hedges, mixed native stand)
blocked.species: Platanus hybrida Brot., Taxus baccata var. fastigiata, Buxus sempervirens L., plus a mixed native conjunto
blocked.register_ref: portugal-icnf.json, 5 entries at Quinta do Senhor da Serra / Paco de Belas, classified as Public Interest Arborescence by the Direcao-Geral das Florestas in 2001; ages 100-200, girths 2.1-4.35m where recorded (cluster_register.py groups them at 0.3km across)
blocked.reason: Private property, access by appointment only: jardinshistoricos.pt states plainly for this quinta 'Privada' / 'Entrada paga / Acesso por marcao' with a contact email and phone to arrange a visit (qsserra@gmail.com, 00351214310038). Confirmed independently: the estate is currently marketed as a residential property (savills.pt listing) and operates as a wedding/event venue (quintasparacasamentos.com, noivos.pt, zankyou.pt all list it as a casamentos venue). Fails the first of hard rule 10's three tests (can a visitor get in without asking anyone's permission): an appointment is explicitly required, which the rule names as a 'no' alongside a doorbell or a guard who checks. Also 12.3km from Sintra's town centre with no direct public-transport link found (Belas/Queluz area, a different orbit from the Sintra hill-town cluster the other 5 trees share); would need its own honest day-trip label even if access cleared, which it does not. A WebSearch AI summary claimed 'may be visited 10am-6pm (8pm summer)' with a viewpoint over Castelo dos Mouros and Pena Palace; the actual allaboutportugal.pt page was fetched directly and contains neither claim (no visiting hours, no viewpoint description at all, and a viewpoint over Sintra's castle/palace is geographically implausible from a site 12km away near Belas). Treated as a search-summary fabrication per the standing rule and discarded rather than used.

blocked.register_ref: portugal-icnf.json, 4 entries at Tala - Quinta do Molha Piao; ages 90-250, girths 2.1-3.15m (cluster_register.py groups them at 0.6km across)
blocked.reason: Private property, access by appointment only: jardinshistoricos.pt states 'Privada' / 'Entrada paga /Acesso por marcao' for this quinta too, with a phone and email to book (+351933031370, geral@molhapao.pt). note_2026_09_18:
Verify pass, 2026-09-18 (seventh consecutive deepen pass off passcheck.py --brief sintra, target 20, 5 live). Re-confirmed rather than repeated: the 0.7km castanheiro, 0.8km sobreiro (=sin_002) and 1.5km platano (=sin_003) are all still the same already-published/blocked matches, and the Colares triple-plane, Senhor da Serra cluster, Molha-Pao cluster, coordinate-error row and Cascais/Estoril cluster are all unchanged. The register genuinely has nothing left.

Tried a new angle the six prior passes had not: dendrological reference literature (International Dendrology Society's treesandshrubsonline.org, a serious secondary source independent of both monumentaltrees.com and generic tourism copy) rather than tourism pages or the register. It named several individually documented specimens at Monserrate and Pena that no prior pass had surfaced. **One cleared the bar and is delivered**: the Queensland Kauri of Monserrate (sin_006, data/research/sintra-verified.json), Agathis robusta, girth 713cm (converted from a 2017 dbh figure), age estimated broadly at 145-175 years. Two independent sources: treesandshrubsonline.org itself (citing Franco 1951, a genuine Portuguese botanical paper on cultivated Agathis in Portugal, independent of Monumental Trees) and jardimformoso.blogspot.com (2009), which quotes Gerald Luckhurst, Monserrate's own garden-restoration landscape architect, by name, describing a comparably large second specimen (6m girth). Flagged for identity uncertainty (Luckhurst describes 'two large specimens'; this entry describes the larger/most recently documented one) and for the 2017 recency of the strongest measurement.

Three did not clear the bar, added above under leads/blocked: a Taxodium distichum at Monserrate (33.5m x 1.5m dbh per the same dendrology site, but that specific figure traces to Monumental Trees with no independent second source found this pass; a lead, not blocked, since a future pass may find one), a labelled but unmeasured Podocarpus neriifolius at Pena Palace (too thin, a lead), and the Abies x vasconcellosiana type trees at Pena Park (genuinely fascinating dendrological history, a naturally occurring hybrid fir first described from Sintra material in 1946 and once distributed to European collections, but the source states outright that the original specimens 'had all died by 1995', so this is BLOCKED as a known-dead tree rather than a lead). Also re-checked and left unchanged: the two Tanque dos Frades sequoias (still no measurement, still species-conflicted between sources, moved into the formal leads list rather than sitting only in prose).

Honest state: Sintra moves from 5 to 6 trees this pass, its first gain since it shipped. The register is fully exhausted and confirmed so seven times now; the remaining path to the 20-tree target is dendrological literature and possibly a future browser-session read of monumentaltrees.com's Monserrate page (still 403 to curl/WebFetch, unresolved since 2026-08-22), not more register or tourism-page sweeps.
note_2026_09_13:
Verify pass, 2026-09-13 (deepen pass off passcheck.py --brief sintra, target 20, 5 live). Sixth consecutive pass to reach the same conclusion. Re-confirmed by distance/field match, independently of the file, that the register within Sintra's day-trip reach is exhausted: the 0.7km castanheiro is the already-blocked mutilated private tree, the 0.8km sobreiro and 1.5km platano are sin_002/sin_003 (~38-45m off, same girths/ages/decrees), and the Colares triple-plane, Senhor da Serra cluster, Molha-Pao cluster, coordinate-error row and Cascais/Estoril cluster are all still correctly blocked or out-of-town. Wikidata's unjudged candidates are all the same Tala/Molha-Pao and Ribeira de Caparide rows already blocked above, 9-19km out.

Spent the remainder of the window on general web research for individually named, measured specimens in Sintra's parks, on angles the five prior passes had not tried, since CLAUDE.md's 'ask which trunk is worth the visit' points there once the register is exhausted. None cleared the bar; recorded here so a seventh pass does not re-walk the same ground:

1. serradesintra.net/grandes-arvores/, a page whose title promised exactly the kind of naming-body source BRIEF_RESEARCH.md looks for first: fetched directly, and the only individually named tree on it is 'Feteira da Rainha', which is a PLACE (the fern valley in Parque da Pena, a recanto), not a single tree. No other specimen on the page carries a name, measurement or coordinate.
2. Monserrate's other official 'recantos' pages beyond the already-published Araucaria/relvado one (Jardim do Mexico, Vale dos Fetos) fetched directly: both describe plant collections and terracing generically (dragon trees, yuccas, tree ferns, cycads) with no individual specimen named, measured or dated. No new candidate.
3. Parque da Pena's own Feteira da Rainha recanto page (parquesdesintra.pt) fetched directly: mentions a 'tuia-gigante' (likely the same species as the already-published sin_001, possibly sin_001 itself referenced generically from a different official page, since no distinguishing detail separates it from the walking tree) and unmeasured deciduous oaks lining the valley. A secondary travel article (viagens.sapo.pt) separately claims 'two enormous sequoias' near Tanque dos Frades in the same general area, said to be among the first specimens from the mid-19th-century reforestation, but the official parquesdesintra.pt page for that exact recanto does not mention sequoias at all, so the two sources conflict on species rather than corroborate each other. No individual measurement, age or coordinate for either sequoia. Genuinely too thin to verify as a candidate (no name, no pin, conflicting species claims); left as an open lead rather than pursued further, worth a future pass if the official page is ever updated or a register/inventory names them individually.
4. Convento dos Capuchos checked again, deliberately this time against the direct page rather than a search summary: a WebSearch AI summary claimed an individually described 'old ash tree in the entrance patio' and 'leafy plane tree covering the convent courtyard'. Per the standing search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule, both parquesdesintra.pt's own Convento dos Capuchos page and the English Wikipedia article were fetched directly to check this, and NEITHER mentions any such ash or plane tree; both describe only the general oak/shrub forest and granite boulders. Treated as a search-summary fabrication and discarded, consistent with the Cyprus-olive case this rule is named for. Recorded here specifically so this false lead is not chased again.
5. Jardim da Preta at Palacio Nacional de Sintra checked (a title that sounded promising for a legend-bearing tree): it is a viewpoint garden named for a Moorish-woman legend, not a tree at all. Not a candidate.

No verified trees delivered this pass; data/research/sintra-verified.json not created since nothing verified. The honest state is unchanged from 2026-09-10: Sintra's register and its most-written-about named specimens are exhausted at the current evidence bar, and its five published trees may represent close to its honest ceiling unless a future pass gets working access to monumentaltrees.com's Monserrate page (still 403 to curl/WebFetch, unresolved since 2026-08-22) or finds a source that individually names and measures a Sintra sequoia, ash or box specimen.
note_2026_09_10:
Verify pass, 2026-09-10, off passcheck.py --brief sintra (deepen pass, target 20, 5 live). Fourth consecutive verify pass to reach the same conclusion, this time independently re-derived rather than trusted from the file: the ICNF register within Sintra's day-trip reach has nothing left. Re-confirmed by distance/field match that the 0.8km sobreiro and 1.5km platano are sin_002 and sin_003 respectively (same girths, ages, decrees as the register rows, ~38-45m off). Re-confirmed the castanheiro, Colares triple-plane, Senhor da Serra cluster and Molha-Pao cluster are still correctly blocked; found one new class of register rows in the brief's 20km radius that were never actually Sintra's to begin with (the Cascais/Estoril cluster, added above) and confirmed they sit unclaimed in lisbon.json too.

Spent the remainder of the window on general web research for individually named specimens in Sintra's famous parks and gardens, since the register is exhausted and CLAUDE.md's 'ask which trunk is worth the visit' principle points there next. Four checked, none new:

1. Quinta da Regaleira's sequoia (mentioned in stock-photo captions and a Facebook video title as 'Sequoia. Parque de Quinta da Regaleira') has no age, no girth, no official page naming or measuring it as an individual specimen (regaleira.pt's own garden page 404s at the URL tried). Same 'too vague' conclusion as 2026-08-22, re-confirmed rather than newly found. Genuinely thin, not pursued further this pass.
2. Parque da Pena's wider arboretum: the one individually named tree found, 'O Gigante da Pena' / 'a árvore que anda' (Thuja plicata, ~35m, said to be one of the park's oldest, walks/leans across the path), is the SAME tree as the already-published sin_001 (The Walking Tree of Pena, Thuja plicata) under its Portuguese nickname. Confirmed by species and the identical 'walking tree' story on parquesdesintra.pt's own blog (parquesdesintra.pt/pt/sobre-nos/blog/sabia-que-no-parque-da-pena-existe-uma-arvore-que-caminha/). Not a new tree; useful as an additional official source for sin_001's story if a future writing pass wants it, not delivered as a verify object since nothing about sin_002 through sin_005's format needs re-verifying.
3. Monserrate's Araucaria heterophylla, named on Parques de Sintra's own official species page (ph30.parquesdesintra.pt/post/monserrate-especies-botanicas, fetched directly) as 'a árvore mais alta da propriedade' at the 'fundo do relvado' (back lawn), height up to 50m: this is the SAME tree as the already-published sin_004 (The Araucaria of Monserrate, 'near the lake', story already states 'over 50 metres tall... by most measurements the tallest tree in the entire garden'). Confirmed duplicate, not a new tree. monumentaltrees.com's Quinta de Monserrate page (which independently lists individual specimens including two named Pohutukawa, likely sin_005) could not be fetched this pass: 403 to plain curl and to curl with a browser user agent alike, consistent with the known Cloudflare gate recorded elsewhere in this project; a browser-session fetch was not available. Worth a future pass with browser access, but the official Parques de Sintra page above already answers the Araucaria question independently.
4. Convento dos Capuchos: every source describes the surrounding oak woodland collectively ('seculos-old trees', 'submediterranean oak formation') as the primitive forest of the Serra de Sintra. No individually named or measured specimen found. Same non-collectible-point shape as the already-blocked Colares avenue and the municipal tilia/platano conjuntos recorded in the 2026-08-28 note; not added as a new blocked entry since it never reached candidate status (no name, no coordinate, no measurement to record).

The honest state of Sintra's supply: the register is exhausted, the day-trip-radius candidates that exist are either already published or already correctly blocked, and Sintra's most-written-about individual specimens (the walking tuia, the Norfolk araucaria, the two Monserrate pohutukawa, the Quinta do Relogio cork oak, the Parque da Liberdade plane) are precisely the 5 already live. Reaching the 20-tree target for Sintra needs either a source this pass could not reach (monumentaltrees.com's Monserrate page via a real browser session, or the treefinder.parquesdesintra.pt database, which is Monserrate-only and currently lists no individual specimens by name despite being built for exactly that), or accepting that Sintra's honest ceiling under the current bar may sit near 5-6 rather than 20. No verified trees delivered this pass; data/research/sintra-verified.json not created since nothing verified.
note_2026_08_22: Verify pass, 2026-08-22: re-checked the full 16-entry Sintra-concelho ICNF register (not just the passcheck brief's 20km-radius list, which mixes in unrelated Lisbon/Monsanto rows already handled by lisbon.json). Every entry is now accounted for: 2 published (sin_002, sin_003), 1 already-blocked private/mutilated tree, 1 already-blocked non-collectible ensemble (Colares), 2 newly-checked clusters now blocked for private/appointment-only access (9 register rows total), and 1 register coordinate error. note_2026_08_28:
Verify pass, 2026-08-28 (deepen pass off passcheck.py --brief sintra). Re-confirmed the 2026-08-22 finding rather than repeating it: of the brief's 34 unmined register candidates, the two flagged 'within 80m of a live tree' are confirmed duplicates of sin_002 and sin_003 (same conclusion as 2026-08-22, re-derived independently by distance calculation, ~32-45m apart, species/girth/age match), the 4.2km Colares triple-plane and everything past 8.6km (Monsanto, Restelo, Belas, Ajuda) are the already-blocked or Lisbon-owned entries this file and lisbon.json already carry, and nothing new sits in between. No new register candidate exists for Sintra. Spent the rest of the pass on the general-web lead the 2026-08-22 note left open (municipal 'Arvores Classificadas' listings) rather than re-running the exhausted register or Wikipedia-join technique (Portugal has no equivalent municipal-register Wikipedia article for Sintra). Two findings, neither delivered as a new tree:

1. sintraromantica.net/pt/visitar/arvores-classificadas (the Camara Municipal de Sintra's own classified-trees page, fetched directly, iso-8859-1, 200 OK) lists every municipally classified tree/ensemble in Sintra concelho. All of them are numbered, unnamed group entries under a site heading (Conjunto de Tilias frente ao Hotel Paris, 19 trees; an unheaded Volta do Duche-area group of platanos/celtis/freixo, ~18 trees; Conjunto de Tilias no Largo D. Manuel I, 19 trees; Conjunto Arboreo do Largo D. Fernando II, reported only as an averaged estimate across the group, not a single tree; Jardim do Rouxinol in Rio de Mouro, 11 numbered platanos plus 2 named-but-generic 'centenary' specimens). None is a single collectible point per the standing rule (same failure as the already-blocked Colares avenue): they are avenues and squares of many same-species trees with no single obvious place to stand at one tree, and the page gives no name distinguishing any individual specimen within a group. Not added to blocked as separate entries since they fail the identical, already-documented test as Colares; recorded here so a future pass does not re-fetch this page expecting different results. One single-specimen exception on the page, a wisteria ('Glicinias do Miradouro da Correnteza', trunk diameter 1.00m, no age given) at a named viewpoint: not pursued this pass, a liana rather than a tree and thin (one measurement, no age, no second source), left as a thin future lead rather than researched to a verdict.

2. The same municipal page's intro text names a specific, individually famous plane tree: 'Grande Maior', the literary nickname Sintra-resident writer Maria Gabriela Llansol gave a plátano at Volta do Duche in her book 'Parasceve', which the Camara Municipal de Sintra physically marked with a plaque at the tree ('esta arvore e universalmente conhecida e na Volta do Duche esta assinalada pela Camara Municipal de Sintra'); WebSearch results independently describe a 2009 municipal recognition of public interest for 'o platano da Volta do Duche' tied to the same Llansol connection. Checked whether this is a genuinely new tree before treating it as one: Nominatim geocodes Volta do Duche (OSM way 23688927, 38.7964784,-9.3866042) at 75m from sin_003's published coordinate (38.796,-9.386, The Plane Tree of Parque da Liberdade), well inside the project's own 80m near-duplicate threshold, and both are the same species (Platanus x acerifolia / hybrida), same general kind of claim (a giant, municipally designated plane tree at this one corner of central Sintra), with no source describing two separate giant planes in this small area. Concluded this is very likely the SAME tree as sin_003 under its literary nickname, not a second tree, so it is not delivered as a new candidate (would risk exactly the duplicate-entry pitfall this file exists to avoid) and not added to blocked (nothing wrong with it, it just is not a new tree). Recorded here instead as a lead for a future STORY pass on sin_003 rather than a verify pass: sin_003's story currently says nothing about Llansol, 'Parasceve', the 'Grande Maior' nickname or the municipal plaque, all of which are genuine, sourced, additive facts about the same already-published tree (sources: sintraromantica.net's classified-trees page for the plaque/attribution claim, and independent WebSearch results referencing a 2009 municipal public-interest recognition for the same tree, which a future pass should verify against a primary Boletim Municipal source before adding a specific date to the story, since the 1951 decree already in sin_003 and this 2009 reference may describe two different administrative acts about the one tree). No coordinate change recommended: sin_003's pin stays as is.
